blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how pilots and sailors navigate across the vast oceans and skies? They rely on a system of latitude and longitude to pinpoint exact locations on Earth.

blocks.markdown: Latitude and longitude are the two coordinates used to locate any point on the Earth's surface. These coordinates form a grid system that helps in navigation and mapping.

blocks.title: Definitions
blocks.text: Latitude: The angular distance of a place north or south of the Earth's equator. Longitude: The angular distance of a place east or west of the Greenwich meridian.

blocks.markdown: The Equator is an imaginary line around the middle of the Earth, equidistant from the North and South Poles. The Greenwich Meridian (Prime Meridian) is the meridian at which longitude is defined to be 0°.
Parallels of latitude are circles parallel to the Equator. Meridians of longitude are half-circles that run from the North Pole to the South Pole.

blocks.title: Finding Coordinates
blocks.prompt: Determine the coordinates of Lagos on a globe.

steps.text: Locate Lagos on the map. It is in Nigeria, on the west coast of Africa.
Find the latitude by measuring the angular distance from the Equator. Lagos is approximately 6.5°N.
Find the longitude by measuring the angular distance from the Greenwich Meridian. Lagos is approximately 3.4°E.

blocks.answer: The coordinates of Lagos are approximately 6.5°N, 3.4°E.

blocks.markdown: Understanding the difference between parallels and meridians is crucial. Parallels run east-west and are equidistant from each other, while meridians run north-south and converge at the poles.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always remember: Latitude is measured in degrees north or south of the Equator, while longitude is measured in degrees east or west of the Greenwich Meridian.

points: Latitude and longitude are used to locate places on Earth.
Latitude lines are parallel to the Equator, while longitude lines converge at the poles.
